clue.text: Hapless broadcaster initially going after all-naked pub and club act

the first letter of the broadcaster's name departs

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: An unfortunate presenter turns up at a pub after a nude club act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-naked' applies to each of the four words in turn. Sky is a British TV broadcaster, and only its first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hapless is unfortunate, dogged by bad luck.

clue.text: Tool modifying iTunes with lead to laptop

indicators.note: modifying the word changes its letter order
the leading letter of laptop

explanation.surface: A tool for tweaking the iTunes app from a laptop.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement or tool, usually for the kitchen.

clue.text: Deputy locked up my half of everything

indicators.note: the first half of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: A stand-in locks away half of the speaker's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: LOC from locked, U from up, M from my.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a temporary stand-in, especially for a doctor or cleric.

clue.text: Suffer punishment from second flier — look out

indicators.note: out says these letters are left out

parts.note: the co-pilot is the second pilot on a flight
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: A shout warning about the second plane, which will be punished.
explanation.walkthrough: COPILOT without LO. Cop it is British slang for being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to cop it is to get into trouble or be punished.

clue.text: Speak up over His Majesty: King supporting a cover-up

indicators.note: the reversed word sits above the royal letters
in a down answer the King letter is below and holds up the a
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to say is to speak
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Speaking up about the King and a royal cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' sounds like a scandal, but it is a veil.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is the veil worn by some Muslim women to cover the face in public.

clue.text: Marx wasting hour visiting business with liberal idea to mobilise workers?

indicators.note: one piece goes to stay inside the other, as a visitor is inside a house

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the letter for hour is dropped

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers

explanation.surface: Karl Marx-style talk of a liberal scheme to mobilise the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx is not Karl but his comedian namesake Harpo. The question mark flags the pun on 'mobilise': putting workers in cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing a car to the office gets commuters moving together, a scheme that literally makes staff mobile.

clue.text: Protection from copper, quiet before one's charged

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the charged one

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
sh is a call for quiet
an ion is an atom or particle carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Protection from a policeman, and silence before one is charged.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion softens a blow, giving padding and so protection.

clue.text: Necessary introduction to riding on horse — sit in knight's place

indicators.note: in a down answer, R sits on top of the rest
the opening letter of riding
sit goes in where the knight was
in someone's place means substituting for them

parts.note: equine as a noun means a horse
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: Riding lessons: sitting on a horse in the knight's position.
explanation.walkthrough: Equine is used as a noun for a horse; in a down clue 'on' puts the first letter above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something requisite is required, needed for a purpose.

clue.text: I tape over wound in action

indicators.note: wound as in twisted, so the letters are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: Taping over a wound received in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Operative means functioning or in force, so in operation.

clue.text: I eat noodles, originally to break religious fast — it's tolerant

indicators.note: the initials break into the fast, splitting it

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Eating noodles to break a religious fast is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' covers all three words, I, eat and noodles, not just the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient person is merciful and forgiving, tolerant of faults.

clue.text: Dreamers in space organised time aboard research satellite

indicators.note: the letters of space are sorted into a new order
time travels inside the satellite, like a passenger aboard

parts.note: ISS is the International Space Station, an orbiting research craft

explanation.surface: Astronauts drifting through space on an orbiting research station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space' tempts as part of the astronaut picture, but it is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapists retreat into fantasy, so they are daydreamers avoiding reality.

clue.text: Piece from burlesque entertainer

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within these words, straddling the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An extract from a burlesque performer's act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a piece of the show, but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen is the most powerful chessman on the board.

clue.text: After evacuation, safety instruction to reader to keep two metres apart is characteristic of illness

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of safety remain
the two Ms hold the reader's instruction between them
the metres are kept apart, one each side

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for metre, so two of them
PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page

explanation.surface: Covid-era safety advice: after evacuating, stand two metres apart.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO (please turn over) is the note to a reader at the foot of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign or feature indicating disease.

clue.text: Angry at time I take off

indicators.note: letters in an angry state are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone furious at being timed decides to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests departing, but here it is mimicking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or impersonate them.

clue.text: Will finally drag in cooker as romantic gift

indicators.note: only the last letter of Will is used
the drag is drawn in, inside the cooker

parts.note: an oven is a cooker
a toke is a drag on a cigarette or joint

explanation.surface: A will leaves a stove, dragged in, as a curious romantic present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag in' reads as a phrase, but drag is the smoker's puff and 'in' places it inside the cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A love token is a keepsake given as a sign of affection.

clue.text: Content to supervise on account of medium or, perhaps, short measure

indicators.note: the content is the inside, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: to oversee is to supervise
for can mean because of
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Managing a medium who gives short measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short measure' is not a cheat but a hymn metre; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Short measure, or short metre, is a hymn stanza pattern, one kind of poetic metre.

clue.text: Sign outside of the man's book

indicators.note: the star sign sits outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
he's contracts he is, the man is

explanation.surface: A zodiac sign on the cover of a man's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The man's' is read as the contraction for 'the man is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms.

clue.text: Heartless sod after filling in his nana

indicators.note: the turf piece comes after the filling
the filling of the word his is its middle letter

parts.note: his middle letter

indicators.note: the middle letter of the turf word is cut out

parts.note: a divot is a piece of sod or turf

explanation.surface: A spiteful remark about grandma filling in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod is not the insult but turf. 'Nana' is British slang for a fool, not a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nana is a fool or silly person, so an idiot.

clue.text: You are caught during escape from the east — blast

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside the other
read from the east is right to left, so backwards

parts.note: ESC is the Escape key on a keyboard
text-speak UR sounds like you are

explanation.surface: You are caught fleeing eastward, and blast it.
explanation.walkthrough: ESC is the keyboard Escape key; 'from the east' means read right to left in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast and curse are both exclamations of annoyance, swearing words.

clue.text: Storm starts in 5,4,3,2,1

indicators.note: the first letters of the answers to these numbered clues

parts.note: the answer to 5 down
the answer to 4 down
the answer to 3 down
the answer to 2 down
1 written as a word

explanation.surface: A countdown, as to a storm breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The countdown numbers are clue references: initials of 5, 4, 3 and 2 down give CYCL, and the final 1 is just ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a violent tropical storm with winds rotating round a centre.

clue.text: 007's boss popular with Bond — new to area that's often consumed with case?

parts.note: M is James Bond's chief in the spy novels
in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: new is changed to area, one letter swapping for the other

parts.note: cement is a bond, something that binds

explanation.surface: James Bond, his boss M and a popular case to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is not 007 but the binding agent CEMENT, whose N becomes A. Mincemeat is the fruit filling eaten in a pastry case, as in a mince pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the sweet fruit filling of mince pies, eaten inside a pastry shell.

clue.text: Knock back some of the raw lamb — it could damage your system

indicators.note: Knock back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Swallowing raw lamb could upset your digestive system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'System' suggests the gut, but it is a computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: Malware is malicious software designed to harm computers.

clue.text: Short letter reviewing TV fundraiser: "Hearts not in it."

indicators.note: the hearts letter is not to be found in the result, so it is removed
re-viewing, looking back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a telethon is a long charity broadcast
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A short note reviewing a charity telethon whose heart wasn't in it.
explanation.walkthrough: TELETHON reversed is NOHTELET; drop the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for a brief note.

clue.text: Smartest One Day International match is entertaining

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or take in, so the match holds the other letters

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The smartest one-day international match is entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Day International' looks like a cricket format, but each word is a letter, I D I, inside TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiest means neatest, the most smart in appearance.

clue.text: Gather around auction site, spending last of money to get essential item for the table

indicators.note: the gathering word goes around the auction site

indicators.note: spending means using up, so a letter goes

parts.note: eBay is an online auction website

indicators.note: the final letter of money

parts.note: money ends in Y

explanation.surface: Collecting goods online, running out of cash, buying something for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The table is a snooker or pool table, not a dining one.
explanation.definitionFit: The white cue ball is struck with the cue in every shot of snooker or pool.

clue.text: Overdraft arranged reflected experimental environment

indicators.note: a mirror image runs backwards

parts.note: an overdraft is a debt to the bank
set means arranged

explanation.surface: Banking jargon: a sorted-out overdraft as a trial scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBTSET read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A test bed is a setting where new equipment or ideas are tried out.

clue.text: Singer makes things that may be used by one channel

definitions.text: Singer makes things that may be used by one
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who sews uses a Singer sewing machine
second meaning: a drain carrying waste water

explanation.walkthrough: Singer is not a vocalist but the sewing-machine brand.

clue.text: Diva removing shell of every nut

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, bonce means the head, which is also called the nut.

clue.text: Occasionally good to query smell

indicators.note: only now and then is a letter used, so every other letter

explanation.surface: It's sometimes worth asking about a smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of good to query.

clue.text: Stint in quirky local drinking pale ale at the end

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in the pale word, as a drinker takes in drink

clue.text: As one worried Essex man must cast vote

explanation.definitionFit: En masse means all together, as a single body.

clue.text: Stream or boring river
